newsitem.title: UK: UK chocolate maker giving politicians a licking.
newsitem.headline: UK chocolate maker giving politicians a licking.

text.p: A British chocolate maker is giving voters a chance to take a bite out of their favourite -- or perhaps their least favourite -- politician with the sale of special election lollipops.

Thorntons, which has about 500 shops throughout Britain, this week introduced chocolate lollipops featuring the heads of Conservative Prime Minister John Major and Labour leader Tony Blair. Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown and Raving Loony leader Screaming Lord Sutch also have lollipops they can call their own.
"It's a very light-hearted look at the elections," Thorntons spokesman Graham Paskett told Reuters on Wednesday.

Thorntons Plc, based in Somercotes, Derbyshire, introduced the lollipops in its shops this week. There is no special promotion or advertising planned. The lollipops, weighing 35 grams each are on sale for 49 pence (79 cents).

The head of each of the chosen politicians was first carved in wood to create a caricature face. From the carving a cast metal mould was made, followed by the making of the plastic moulds that are used in the actual chocolate production.
In the run-up to the last general election in 1992 Thorntons featured jelly lollipop heads of Major, Ashdown and then-Labour leader Neil Kinnock.
The company sold 170,000 of the jelly lollipops and needed three extra production runs to meet demand. Paskett declined to make any predictions on the sale of this year's confection.
"Our poll isn't designed to predict the general election, but we're sure they'll all get licked," Paskett said.
